task.description:
WF-03 closing gate on the ISS-0198 amendment. The diff under review is `git diff 5a8089e..HEAD` (commits df7f4ad, 83da516). DOC-UPDATER's own report is handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/step-03-amendment.json; the diagnosis it was built from is step-005-01-diagnose.json. Both are in artifacts_in. Read the DIFF, not the reports -- re-derive every verdict from the amended files themselves.

Gate the eleven acceptance criteria on step-03-amendment.json against the diff. Beyond those, five checks this gate exists for:

A. RE-RUN THE MECHANICAL CLAIMS YOURSELF. DOC-UPDATER quotes `json.loads OK; top-level keys: 18`, a corpus scan of `parseable: 585 unparseable: 0 carrying source_text: 0`, and a grep showing zero H-SIZE/6000 hits in core-directives.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md. Accepting a quoted command output is copying a claim. Run them.

B. THE NEW OPTIONAL FIELD. DOC-UPDATER declined to generalise context.requirement_text and added context.source_text instead. Judge the call on its merits, and specifically: does the amended section 2 still say unambiguously WHICH field a given piece of copied text belongs in, such that two agents would put the same text in the same field? An optional slot nobody can decide to use is worse than no slot.

C. THE 'OPTIONAL FIELD' COUNT. Section 2 previously asserted not_agent_attested was 'the one OPTIONAL field'. That sentence is now amended to name two. Verify the amended text is internally consistent with section 4.1(b)'s closed-member-set language, which was itself written this morning and is load-bearing for ISS-0191's linter.

D. AC5 CAME BACK NEGATIVE AND WAS REPORTED HONESTLY. The re-drafted corpus-maximum dispatch went 12,187 -> 7,333 chars with acceptance criteria byte-identical, and STILL flags H-SIZE-1. Check the re-draft yourself. Two questions: is the remaining 7,333 genuinely irreducible without cutting scope (the truncation failure mode H-SIZE-2 guards), and does the amended prose actually say H-SIZE-1 is advisory for this reason -- or does a reader come away thinking 6,000 is a budget? This is the criterion most likely to have been written to look like a pass.

E. SELF-CONSISTENCY. This amendment forbids restating what artifacts_in already names. Does the amendment itself obey the rule it writes, across all three touched docs?

FAIL with specific gaps named per criterion if any check fails. Do not fix anything yourself -- this is a gate. Modify no file outside handoffs/.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict re-derived from the diff itself, with the amended HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 text read directly, not from DOC-UPDATER's summary
Each of the eleven acceptance criteria on step-03-amendment.json is given an explicit PASS or FAIL with the evidence that decided it
The json.loads fence check, the corpus parseability scan, and the core-directives/ORCHESTRATOR grep are re-run first-hand and the actual outputs quoted
Check B answered: the amended section 2 is judged on whether requirement_text vs source_text is decidable by two agents reaching the same answer
Check C answered: the amended optional-field count is consistent with section 4.1(b)'s closed-member-set language
Check D answered: the re-draft is inspected first-hand, and the amended prose is judged on whether it reads as advisory or as a budget
Check E answered: the amendment is checked against its own rule across all three touched docs
Any FAIL names the specific gap and the file/section, never a general impression
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
GATE: PASS. Every verdict below was re-derived from `git diff 5a8089e..HEAD` and the amended files themselves; DOC-UPDATER's result.summary was read only to know what was claimed, never as evidence.

A. MECHANICAL CLAIMS RE-RUN FIRST-HAND (all three reproduce).
(1) Section 2 JSON fence. Extracted every ```json fence from HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and ran json.loads on each. Fence 0 -- the section 2 schema block -- 'OK top-level keys: 18', context keys ['stage','requirement_ids','requirement_text','source_text','related_handoff_ids','artifacts_in','owned_modules']. Matches the quoted claim exactly. (Fences 1-4 are bare "result": {...} illustration fragments and fail json.loads as 'Extra data'; they are pre-existing, untouched by this diff, and were never whole objects. Only fence 0 is the machine-loadable schema.)
(2) Corpus scan. json.load over every *.json under handoffs/ except registry.json: 'parseable: 586 unparseable: 0 carrying source_text: 0'. DOC-UPDATER quoted 585; the delta is step-03b-reviewer-gate.json itself, created after its scan. The field is optional-by-absence and invalidates nothing.
(3) Grep. grep -nE "H-SIZE|6,?000" over docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md -> exit 1, no output. Repo-wide, H-SIZE and 6,000 appear only in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and ISS-0191.yaml. Claim confirmed.
(4) NOT ASKED FOR, RUN ANYWAY, because the 6,000 threshold's whole justification rests on it. Re-derived the corpus statistics over 586 files: median 682.5 (claimed 682), p90 3,180 (claimed 3,191), p95 5,139 (claimed 5,138), max 12,187 (claimed 12,187), 20 files over 6,000 = 3.4% (claimed 20 / 3.4%), and of those 20, 20 name an artifacts_in basename inside their own description (claimed all 20). The percentile deltas are corpus growth plus interpolation method. The percentile justification for 6,000 and the 'cite-and-restate is the entire mechanism' claim both hold on independent measurement.

B. THE NEW OPTIONAL FIELD -- is requirement_text vs source_text decidable? YES for every case the corpus contains, with one narrow edge noted. Section 2 gives a bright line: requirement_text is keyed by REQ-ID and carries a requirement's `description` from docs/requirements.yaml; source_text is keyed by source path and carries 'any other cited source'. Two agents asked where a REQ description goes both answer requirement_text (its contract paragraph is untouched and the new prose says so in terms); asked where an amended clause of a protocol file goes, both answer source_text. The judgement call -- not generalising requirement_text by re-keying it on path -- is the right one and I would have made it: its REQ-ID keying is load-bearing for the 'requirement_ids set + requirement_text missing = malformed' test every role runs, and re-keying would have broken that contract for a benefit a sibling field gets free. EDGE (MINOR, filed below): text copied from docs/requirements.yaml that is NOT a description -- a REQ's acceptance_criteria, say -- falls outside requirement_text's stated contract and so lands in source_text keyed 'docs/requirements.yaml', but an agent could plausibly append it under the REQ-ID key instead. Narrow, not a blocker. The 'when to use it at all' test ('only when the exact text must be in front of the agent -- a clause being amended, a line being quoted back', default absent) is bounded enough to act on, and the AC5 re-draft demonstrates the negative case explicitly, which is better evidence that it is decidable in practice than any amount of prose.

C. THE OPTIONAL-FIELD COUNT vs SECTION 4.1(b). CONSISTENT -- the two statements have disjoint, explicitly stated scopes. Section 2 says 'Exactly two fields IN THE BLOCK ABOVE are OPTIONAL', scoped to the schema fence. Section 4.1(b) says the not_agent_attested OBJECT's member set 'is CLOSED at those seven, and backfill_note is the only optional one', scoped to that object's members. Read the fence directly: its not_agent_attested object carries exactly the six required members and no backfill_note, so section 2's count is true of the block as written and does not collide with 4.1(b). 4.1(b)'s decidable membership test -- the thing ISS-0191's linter needs -- is untouched by this diff (verified: the backfill_note lines are identical at 5a8089e and HEAD).
OBSERVATION, filed below as MINOR and NOT gating: section 2 declares the fence the machine-loadable schema, and the fence has no backfill_note, while 4.1(b) legitimises exactly one existing file that carries it. That gap pre-dates this amendment (it arrived with 4.1(b) in c6ec3c1, an ancestor of the base commit). This amendment does not widen it, but it does add an emphatic 'neither licenses a third', which a linter author skimming section 2 could over-read as 'no third optional key anywhere in the schema' and then reject the one authorised backfill_note file. Cheap to close with a cross-reference clause. Not a defect in what was written -- a seam between two sections written a day apart.

D. AC5 CAME BACK NEGATIVE AND WAS REPORTED HONESTLY -- CONFIRMED, and it is the strongest part of the amendment. Measured the re-draft myself rather than reading its table: the source file's task.description is 12,187 chars and its 8 acceptance_criteria total 1,589; the re-draft's fenced description is 7,333. Every figure reproduces. The claim that step-02b-code-design-validator.json was restated at length while not being listed also reproduces -- it is absent from the original's artifacts_in (9 paths, checked).
IS THE REMAINING 7,333 IRREDUCIBLE WITHOUT CUTTING SCOPE? Read both descriptions side by side. What went is the five things claimed and only those: Step 1's diagnosis paragraph, Step 1's specific lead, Step 2b's what-the-gate-confirmed block, Step 2b's blocking-defect narrative with its quoted tenant.ex:56 line and changeset error, and the per-issue one-liners for ISS-0110/0111/0113/0107. What survives is instruction: the read-first ordering, the if-REAL/if-NOT branch with its SECURITY-REVIEWER consequence, scope items (A)(B)(C) intact, ISS-0112's binding two-modules instruction intact, both mandatory design sections, all four constraints including the toolchain note and the never-`git add -A` line, and both MINOR gate items. I could not find a further 1,333 chars to remove that is not instruction. The claim is sound.
DOES THE PROSE READ AS ADVISORY OR AS A BUDGET? ADVISORY, said in more than one voice so a skimmer cannot miss it: section 2 -- 'No target length is stated here or anywhere, and none is to be inferred from the WARN threshold ... that threshold selects a tail for reporting, it is not a budget any dispatch must meet'; Enforcement note -- '6,000 is a WARN threshold, not a length any dispatch is required to meet' and 'Both WARN checks are advisory by design', with section 6 ('never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures') named as the reason neither is hard; and H-SIZE-2 is explicitly framed as the check that fires on the truncation a budget reading would produce. The negative AC5 result is the load-bearing evidence for all of it, and it is reported in the artefact, in result.summary and in issues[0]. This is the criterion I expected to have been written to look like a pass; it was not.

E. SELF-CONSISTENCY across the three touched docs. OBEYED. core-directives.md gets four lines that point at section 2 and say 'deliberately not restated here'; ORCHESTRATOR.md gets four lines that say 'That section is canonical and this line does not restate it'; neither names the threshold, the check IDs, or any row of the table (grep-confirmed above). ISS-0191.yaml points at the Enforcement note and says 'do not re-derive them here'. One intra-file repetition inside the canonical file -- the 9-of-19 rework figure and the 20-files figure appear in both section 2's rationale and the Enforcement note -- which is the same file, not a second one, so the no-duplication constraint holds. Noted, not charged.

ELEVEN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA -- explicit verdicts.
AC1 six changes + seventh: PASS. Diagnosis items 1-6 all land (section 2 rule; Enforcement note H-SIZE-1/2/3; core-directives pointer; ORCHESTRATOR pointer; ISS-0191 scope; no target length). Item 1's 'generalising the structured copied-source slot beyond docs/requirements.yaml' is satisfied by a sibling field rather than by re-keying -- see B. The seventh change is present in ISS-0198.yaml.
AC2 canonical marker, ORCHESTRATOR section 10 wording shape, adjacent to requirement_text: PASS. Section 10 reads 'This section is the canonical definition of the direct-action exception. Other files point here; none of them restates the test. Do not re-derive it from "is this trivial?"'; the new subsection reads 'This subsection is the canonical definition of the handoff structure rule. Other files point here; none of them restates it. Do not re-derive it from "is this dispatch too long?"' Same shape, three sentences, same order. It begins at line 170, immediately after the requirement_text paragraph ending at 167.
AC3 inline-vs-artifacts_in distinction: PASS. Two-column table, four rows a side, plus 'When content on the right is also reproduced on the left, the reproduction is the defect' and a worked cite-do-not-restate example.
AC4 H-SIZE-1/2/3 computable + ISS-0191 scope + ISS-0190 sequencing: PASS. Each check is an expression over json.load/len/substring/basename with no repo state: H-SIZE-1 is len(desc)>6000 AND any(basename in desc), H-SIZE-2 is len(desc)+sum(len(ac))<400, H-SIZE-3 is a report. I evaluated H-SIZE-1 over the whole corpus mechanically with no judgement call required (see A4), which is the operative proof of computability. ISS-0191.yaml's ADDED TO SCOPE block records ISS-0190 as a prerequisite and adds ISS-0198 to related.
AC5 nothing implies the check runs today: PASS. Heading 'Specified but NOT YET RUNNING', opening 'None of these three checks runs today, and nothing in this file should be read as saying otherwise', and ISS-0191.yaml repeats the not-today statement. MINOR: the re-draft artefact's table says H-SIZE-1 'flags' / 'still flags' in the present tense; in context it is the author applying the specified predicate by hand, and the same file calls ISS-0191's linter the thing that WOULD pick files up, so it does not assert the linter exists. Noted, not charged.
AC6 pointer sentences only: PASS. Grep exit 1 on both files; each addition read in full in the diff and contains no row of the table and no threshold.
AC7 weak-model tolerance + requirement-text guarantee preserved with the mechanism stated: PASS. The prose states the mechanism rather than asserting the outcome (no instruction text removed; task/criteria/constraints stay inline; copied source moves from unlabelled prose into a labelled field in the same file; only the second copy goes) and closes with a tie-breaker a weak model can execute -- 'An agent unsure which side of the table a passage falls on writes it inline'. The section 2 guarantee is restated as in force and generalised, not narrowed.
AC8 fence parses, verified and quoted: PASS -- reproduced first-hand, see A1.
AC9 justification on redundancy, no target length as a rule: PASS -- and the underlying measurement reproduces independently, see A4. The prose carries the disclaimer in terms ('The case is not that shorter is faster').
AC10 ISS-0198 figures corrected with attribution: PASS. The MEASURED paragraph now reads TEN files, 8,915, 8,693-41,723 bytes; the original claim is preserved in a corrections block dated, attributed to DOC-UPDATER and this run, sourced to the Step 1 diagnosis, with the unsupported latency premise recorded as item 4. Nothing deleted silently. YAML re-parsed clean.
AC11 AC5 discharged against a real run: PASS -- counts reproduced first-hand, see D.

NO FILE OUTSIDE handoffs/ WAS MODIFIED BY THIS STEP. git status --porcelain was empty before I began writing this handoff, and the only path this step touches is handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json. Nothing was fixed by me; the three MINOR findings below are routed to ORCH, not applied.

issues.description: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 declares its JSON fence the machine-loadable schema and now says 'Exactly two fields in the block above are OPTIONAL ... neither licenses a third', but the fence's not_agent_attested object omits backfill_note, which section 4.1(b) legitimises on exactly one authorised file. The gap pre-dates this amendment (it arrived with 4.1(b) in c6ec3c1, an ancestor of base 5a8089e) and is not widened by it, but the new emphatic closure sentence makes an over-read more likely: a linter author working from section 2 alone could reject the one file that legitimately carries backfill_note. Fix is one cross-reference clause in section 2, or a rule in ISS-0191 that reads 4.1(b) for not_agent_attested's members. Not gating.

context.requirement_text vs context.source_text is decidable for every case the corpus contains, but one edge is unstated: text copied from docs/requirements.yaml that is NOT a requirement's description (a REQ's acceptance_criteria, for instance) falls outside requirement_text's stated contract and so belongs in source_text keyed 'docs/requirements.yaml', while an agent could plausibly append it under the REQ-ID key instead. One clause in section 2 would settle it. Not gating -- the dominant case is unambiguous and source_text's default is absence.

In the AC5 re-draft, the SCOPE--OUT one-line summaries of ISS-0110/0111/0113/0107 were removed as restatement of docs/issues/ISS-01{07,10,11,13}.yaml, but those four issue records are not in the source handoff's artifacts_in (9 paths, none of them an ISS-011x record) and the re-draft does not add them. The structure rule's table says such content 'belongs as a PATH in context.artifacts_in'; naming the IDs inline without listing the paths is a half-application of the rule. The instruction itself survives (the do-not-design-fixes-for-these directive and ISS-0112's binding two-modules clause are both intact), so this is a worked-example imperfection rather than a defect in the rule. Worth a sentence in section 2 making explicit that if a restatement is dropped, the source must appear in artifacts_in -- that is exactly the step a weak model would skip.

result.next_action: Gate PASSED -- the ISS-0198 amendment stands as committed (df7f4ad, 83da516); no rework needed and nothing was changed by this step. ORCH: (1) update handoffs/registry.json for step-03b; (2) file the result.summary-size issue this run was told to leave alone, noting that this step's own summary is again an instance of the pattern; (3) decide whether the three MINOR findings above become docs/issues/ entries or riders on ISS-0191 -- findings 1 and 3 are natural additions to ISS-0191's scope, finding 2 is a one-clause edit to HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2; (4) close the run.
